subject: Operational clarity and corrective roadmap for tokenization event
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@optibank.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@optibank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial notice — tokenization request failure window (Oct 29)

Hi Lina / Tom,

Thank you for raising this with us. I wanted to confirm we've completed the immediate containment steps for the tokenization failures you saw on Oct 29 (service window between 02:12–02:48 UTC). The customer-facing surface has been restored and requests are routing to a stable fallback; we do not see new failed tokenization requests post-containment.

Next steps:
- We're preparing a concise technical summary and action plan for you (ETA: 48 hours).
- We'll include the execution timeline, root cause analysis, and a set of mitigations with owners and target dates.

We recognize this impacted a small percentage of transactions and appreciate your patience — we'll ensure you have artifacts suitable for your compliance review.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: incident-evidence-stub.csv (attachment stub)

From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@optibank.com>

Subject: Re: Initial notice — tokenization request failure window (Oct 29)

Soojin,

Thanks for the prompt note. Two asks from our side: 1) a clear timeline we can include in an internal incident memo, and 2) whether there was any possibility of partial exposure (we need a short statement we can give to our InfoSec team).

Also looping our security inbox (security@optibank.com) for visibility.

Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Nov 2028 08:19:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: OptiBank — timeline and short exposure statement (draft)

Sooj, Jonas — drafting the external summary now. Key technical points for the RCA: intermittent KV-cache eviction under high concurrent prefix loads, exacerbated by a malformed retry from a scheduled ingestion job that burst requests with longer-than-expected sequences. That combination caused tokenization request handlers to hit an untested code path where graceful fallback didn't execute.

I'm attaching an initial brief and the evidence CSV (request IDs and timestamps). I suggest we: 1) validate phrasing for "no data exfiltration" with infra, 2) produce a one-page timeline for Tom, and 3) propose three mitigations (conservative eviction thresholds, retry throttling, and a fallback routing policy).

Attachment: draft-brief-v0.docx (internal)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@optibank.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@optibank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Operational summary & corrective roadmap — tokenization event (concise)

Hi Lina / Tom,

Apologies for the delay — attached is our concise operational summary and corrective roadmap for the Oct 29 tokenization event. Key points up front:

- What happened (summary): A small subset of tokenization requests (0.7% of peak traffic during the window) failed when a combination of a high-concurrency prefix workload and an unusual retry pattern triggered a cache eviction path that bypassed the intended graceful fallback.
- Impact: Failed tokenizations were limited to requests matching the ingestion pattern; we have verified no plaintext payment data left Redwood systems.
- Root cause (short): Interaction between KV cache eviction policy and a burst of longer sequence requests from a scheduled ingestion job.

Actions we are committing to (owners & dates):
1) Conservative cache eviction thresholds and telemetry gating — owner: infra (Jonas Weber) — ETA: 2028-11-28
2) Retry-throttling at the ingestion edge and validation of ingestion job backoff — owner: platform (Marissa Cole) — ETA: 2028-11-22
3) Fallback routing rule: route tokenization to the verified safe path on anomalies — owner: serving runtime (Jonas Weber) — ETA: 2028-11-21
4) Compliance artifact: evidence log and signed statement for your InfoSec — owner: account team (Soojin Lee) — ETA: 2028-11-15

Files attached: 20281115-tokenization-brief.pdf (summary + timeline), evidence-log-20281110.csv (request ids and checksums), mitigation-playbook.md

Please let us know if you'd like a short review call (20 min) this week to walk through the timeline and controls. We're ready to join Tom's InfoSec review if helpful.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Park <lina.park@optibank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@optibank.com>, security@optibank.com
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational summary & corrective roadmap — tokenization event

Soojin — thanks for the thorough note and attachments. Quick confirmation from our side: the one-page timeline looks fine for our internal memo. A couple of follow-ups: 1) For the "no plaintext data left" statement, could you provide the short verification steps your infra team used? We need enough detail to include in our audit log. 2) Can you confirm whether the mitigation timelines above are blocking for our migration scheduled Dec 5 — we need assurance there won't be recurring failures if we proceed.

Would prefer a short call tomorrow (Nov 16) at 10:00 AM PT to go through the verification steps and mitigation sequencing.

Thanks,
Lina

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@optibank.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@optibank.com>, security@optibank.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operational summary & corrective roadmap — tokenization event

Lina / Tom — confirming the call for Nov 16, 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). For your two asks:

1) Verification steps summary (short):
- We reviewed request logs and checksums for the affected request IDs (attached CSV); compared tokenization outputs to internal hash manifests; verified no matches to plaintext storage snapshots taken per retention policy.
- We executed targeted replays in a controlled environment to validate that inputs do not result in accidental persistence.
- Infra validated access logs during the window (no elevated read permissions or external egress).

2) Migration risk: With the short-term mitigations (retry-throttling and fallback routing) in place (ETA Nov 21–22), we do not expect recurrence of this class of failure during your Dec 5 migration. Jonas and Marissa will be on the call to confirm sequencing and be available for a short technical pre-check on Nov 28 if you want a dry run.

Attached: 20281115-tokenization-brief.pdf, evidence-log-20281110.csv, mitigation-playbook.md

Thanks — we'll be prepared to provide the formal signed statement for your audit on the call.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

--
Internal note: marissa and jonas — per call, prioritize the fallback routing config (Jonas) and ingestion throttling (Marissa). I'll collect signoff and produce the signed compliance artifact after verification.
